### Extreme-shape probability evaluation

Large-shape beta-prime densities require the beta normalizer before the nearly equal log-gamma terms are subtracted. The probability-only normalizer uses the shifted gamma ratio; it leaves the fitter normalizer unchanged. At a symmetric median the inverse retains the original probability offset, rather than subtracting two rounded log tails.

The concentrating symmetric tail uses t=log(x/scale), with a=shape1=shape2. Rounding its two beta coordinates can erase a resolved displacement. This probability bridge returns NaN for sqrt(a)*E > 2.5e-11 and 0 < |t| < 2E/1e-10, where E is eight binary64 machine epsilons. At t=0 the exact symmetric half-probability remains available; the stated margin is practical floating-point evidence.

When shape2 is one or two, the transformed beta coordinate admits an exact power or power-times-linear CDF. The latter uses a positive-deviance hazard rather than subtracting its nearly equal logarithmic terms, retaining small tails without relying on extended-precision beta normalization.

### Unequal concentrating beta shapes

The density normalizer is centered at the beta mean and combined with two nonnegative Bernoulli deviances. In the unit-power submodel, a compensated product expansion retains shape2 times the physical excess minus shape1 times scale before either ratio rounds; a rounded beta coordinate can lose the entire standardized displacement.

### Far-count beta normalization

The beta factor in the far-count tail prefactor is evaluated through a shifted gamma ratio, avoiding cancellation of large log-gamma values when a mixing shape diverges. This addresses the normalizing factor only; the extreme mixing-tail and quantile limitations recorded by the audit remain separate.

On the uniform mixing submodel (alpha=beta=1), the mass is exactly r/((r+x)(r+x+1)); evaluating this rational identity removes gamma cancellation at arbitrarily large r. Interchangeability of r and beta gives the corresponding symmetric case. The remaining beta=1 path uses a short shifted gamma ratio when its relative shift is at most one half.

### Extreme d/p/q arithmetic

When one count-shape is one, the survival function is the beta ratio B(x+1+r,alpha)/B(r,alpha). Computing it directly avoids complementing a lower sum whose rounding error can exceed the entire upper tail. Positive small gamma increments use log1p in their recurrence. For large-count masses in this submodel, NaN is returned if the estimated subtraction margin 16 epsilon times the sum of absolute log-beta terms exceeds the log-density tolerance.

When alpha and one count-shape are one, the two tails are the exact rational weights (x+1)/(r+x+1) and r/(r+x+1). Their log-odds form avoids subtracting two gamma increments near log(r), whose cancellation can spoil a small natural CDF even when the log-tail absolute error is tiny.

The unit count-shape CDF at zero uses alpha/(alpha+r) directly, including when alpha+r overflows. For counts below the existing 100000-term structural guard, the unit count-shape bridge sums the exact product hazard in scaled, compensated coordinates; its mass uses the preceding survival times alpha/(alpha+r+x). For larger counts the beta-ratio bridge returns NaN if x+1+r rounds back to r, if the practical log-beta subtraction margin exceeds the log-tail tolerance, or if a nonpositive/subnormal computed hazard cannot meet its resolution margin. Mass evaluations whose shape sum overflows the original rising-factorial kernel also return NaN. These named precision regions prevent a rounded beta-ratio difference from being reported as an exact zero probability.

### Concentrating probability coordinates

At large power, forming x-min first can erase the displacement from min+scale. Evaluation retains that center and its addition residual before forming the log ratio. The density groups the two beta-tail penalties separately, avoiding cancellation between the power term and their shared softplus. Inversion transports the log displacement through expm1 before adding the location; otherwise min=-scale can lose the entire quantile.

The concentrating symmetric tail uses t=shape2*log((x-min)/scale), with a=shape1=shape3. Rounding its two beta coordinates can erase a resolved displacement. This probability bridge returns NaN for sqrt(a)*E > 2.5e-11 and 0 < |t| < 2E/1e-10, where E is eight binary64 machine epsilons. At t=0 the exact symmetric half-probability remains available; the stated margin is practical floating-point evidence.

The shape1 one/two reductions use the closed beta-coordinate tails rather than a promoted backend normalizer. At shape1 two, the positive-deviance hazard described in [the GB2 dossier](../gb2/README.md#probability-coordinates-at-large-power) is applied after the translated power coordinate; both translation and the tail calculation must retain their low-order terms.

### Unequal concentrating beta shapes

The density normalizer is centered at the beta mean and combined with two nonnegative Bernoulli deviances. In the unit-power submodel, a compensated product expansion retains shape2 times the physical excess minus shape1 times scale before either ratio rounds; a rounded beta coordinate can lose the entire standardized displacement. For other powers, the log-odds kernel returns NaN near concentration when its practical coordinate-error margin exceeds 1e-12 times the log-density scale. This named precision region requires more accurate transcendental coordinates to close.

If the ordinary log-odds margin fails, two-word logarithms recompute the centered coordinate before rounding. The beta mean is subtracted in the same arithmetic. NaN remains confined to cases where this practical two-word margin also fails; the ordinary margin selects the recomputation rather than a refusal.

### Concentrating log density

For large shape, a log-gamma subtraction can lose the entire finite density near the mode. The density separates its Stirling normalizer from the nonnegative deviance k*(u-log1p(u)). Binary mantissas and an FMA residual retain the exact scale-times-shape center without overflow or subnormal product loss; the finite Taylor polynomial preserves k*u^2 even when u^2 underflows. The omitted Stirling term is below 3e-17 at the regime boundary.

For shape at least 16, probabilities integrate the centered log-gamma density with the bounded Simpson and log-concave tangent construction also used by the Prentice family. The exact binary64 scale-times-shape center is retained before standardization. The smaller-shape path passes a representable unit-scale argument directly to the gamma backend instead of exponentiating its logarithm. A small FMA division residual is transported through the density; the unresolved region where its relative tail correction exceeds 1e-7 returns NaN. Far from the mode, an explicit log-concave Laplace bound controls the tail remainder by 1e-12. Exhausted series or continued fractions also return NaN.

The inverse can return the mean when Chernoff bounds put the requested quantile within relative 1e-10 of it; a factor-two exponent margin reserves floating-point error. This shortcut returns NaN if that bracket intersects the binary64 overflow boundary. It is confined to the gamma inverse, since further power or exponential transforms can amplify its relative allowance.

### Probability coordinates at large power

A nonunit scale makes subtraction of log(x) and log(scale) lose the displacement amplified by the power. The positive log-ratio helper retains the exact near-scale subtraction. For equal beta shapes, central inversion uses the original probability offset and the bounded local inverse of the symmetric log-odds density.

The concentrating symmetric tail uses t=shape2*log(x/scale), with a=shape1=shape3. Rounding its two beta coordinates can erase a resolved displacement. This probability bridge returns NaN for sqrt(a)*E > 2.5e-11 and 0 < |t| < 2E/1e-10, where E is eight binary64 machine epsilons. At t=0 the exact symmetric half-probability remains available; the stated margin is practical floating-point evidence.

For shape1 = 2, the beta-coordinate CDF is u^shape3 (1 + shape3(1-u)). Its negative logarithm is the sum of two positive logarithmic deviances. Retaining that hazard in log coordinates avoids both a cancelled complement and a backend beta normalizer whose relative error grows at tiny shapes in double-width builds. The one-shape coordinate uses its exact power CDF.

### Unequal concentrating beta shapes

The density normalizer is centered at the beta mean and combined with two nonnegative Bernoulli deviances. In the unit-power submodel, a compensated product expansion retains shape2 times the physical excess minus shape1 times scale before either ratio rounds; a rounded beta coordinate can lose the entire standardized displacement. For other powers, the log-odds kernel returns NaN near concentration when its practical coordinate-error margin exceeds 1e-12 times the log-density scale. This named precision region requires more accurate transcendental coordinates to close.

If the ordinary log-odds margin fails, two-word logarithms recompute the centered coordinate before rounding. The beta mean is subtracted in the same arithmetic. NaN remains confined to cases where this practical two-word margin also fails; the ordinary margin selects the recomputation rather than a refusal.

### Endpoint power

The zero-endpoint classification uses the residual of the exact binary64 shape-times-power product minus one. Rounding that product first can falsely select a finite density when the exact endpoint density is zero or infinite.

For shape2 = 2, write u = (x/scale)^shape3. The CDF u^shape1 (1 + shape1(1-u)) is evaluated through positive logarithmic deviances, with a Taylor remainder bound when the hazard is too small to materialize. This avoids the double-width beta-backend normalization error on reciprocal-power paths. Shape2 one uses the exact power law.

### Concentrating beta coordinates

At unit power the affine beta density retains the physical displacement through compensated products. Other powers use the centered beta log-odds density. Its practical coordinate margin includes amplification by 1/(1-y) when y=(x/scale)^power approaches one. The density returns NaN near concentration if that margin exceeds 1e-12 times its log-density scale; this named precision region requires more accurate transcendental coordinates.

If the ordinary log-odds margin fails, two-word logarithms recompute the centered coordinate before rounding. The beta mean is subtracted in the same arithmetic. The complement uses a direct expm1 series near zero, so forming one minus a rounded exponential cannot erase it. NaN remains confined to cases where this practical two-word margin also fails; the ordinary margin selects the recomputation rather than a refusal.

### Extreme d/p/q arithmetic

The normal inverse retains the offset of a log-probability input from exact log(1/2) before multiplication by sigma. Equality with a rounded logarithmic median is insufficient when sigma is large.

### Thin normal images

A rounded logit can equal the supplied normal mean while their exact difference is nonzero. Dividing that lost residual by a tiny standard deviation changes both density and tails. When the ordinary coordinate margin is too large, a two-word atanh-series logarithm retains the residual before division. The only exact rational logit center, x=1/2, is handled directly. Density and tails return NaN when the stated practical two-word margin still cannot resolve the transformed coordinate; this is the remaining named precision region.

### Translated quantiles and shape extremes

A beta quantile rounded before affine transport can erase a nonzero result when the endpoints straddle zero. Central symmetric inversion retains the offset from one half through the compensated midpoint calculation. The probability normalizer also avoids subtraction of large log-gamma values when one shape diverges.

The concentrating symmetric tail uses t=log((x-min)/(max-x)), with a=shape1=shape2. Rounding its two beta coordinates can erase a resolved displacement. This probability bridge returns NaN for sqrt(a)*E > 2.5e-11 and 0 < |t| < 2E/1e-10, where E is eight binary64 machine epsilons. At t=0 the exact symmetric half-probability remains available; the stated margin is practical floating-point evidence.

The shape2 one/two beta-coordinate reductions retain the cumulative hazard before rescaling the interval. Their closed antiderivatives avoid backend normalizer loss in double-width builds; at shape2 two a positive-deviance sum retains the complement at the upper endpoint.

### Normal-member centering

At nu = 2 the standardized law is exactly the skew-normal member. Its d/p evaluations use the compensated skew-normal moment and residual calculation, including the documented forward-error gate and NaN precision regions in [the skew-normal dossier](../snorm/README.md#extreme-dpq-arithmetic). This preserves the thin-side residual before division by xi² instead of rounding the Gaussian absolute moment inside the generalized-Gaussian calculation.

### Exact base-moment submodel

At nu=1 the standardized base is Laplace, with first absolute moment 1/sqrt(2). Retaining its low word and the skew mean displacement removes the thin-side cancellation that remains after ordinary moment evaluation. The broad-side central mass is -expm1(-sqrt(2)*v), rather than a difference of rounded CDFs. The d/p bridge returns NaN if its practical coordinate margin fails or its raw displacement or standardized radius cannot be represented; these are named precision regions. Sampling and the inverse transformation retain their original arithmetic.

For the other members with representable moments, two-word log-Gamma values retain the standardized first absolute moment before centering. Recurrence reaches arguments of at least 32; the first omitted Stirling term is below 5.2e-35. Its propagated practical moment margin participates in the coordinate gate. The symmetric member delegates directly to GED, and the large-nu radius precision gate remains in force after compensated standardization.

The natural-tail precision region includes nu=3.8792797496374307, xi=1e8, mean=0, sd=1 at x=-1.5461574810135936 and x=-1.5461574810135932. The propagated moment/coordinate margins are respectively 3.165e-10 and 9.167e-11 in the log tail. Natural lower tails return NaN under the reserved 1e-11 coordinate budget; their independently computed probabilities remain in the truth exclusions. Log tails retain their scaled error allowance. A sharper first-moment enclosure could reduce this region.

### Extreme d/p/q arithmetic

For t = min(xi, 1/xi), normalize the centering moment and standard deviation before forming the residual: m(t²-1) and sqrt((1-m²)(1+t⁴)+(2m²-1)t²), where m = sqrt(2/pi). On the thin side the residual is divided by t², so rounding m or its standard deviation first can create order-one errors at xi = 1e-8. Compensated products, sums, division and a square-root correction retain the low-order terms; the moment constant retains its second binary64 component.

The practical centering margin is 64 epsilon² (1+|w|), with eight epsilon times the standardized radius reserved for its final rounding. Density and tail evaluations return NaN when this propagated margin exceeds 1e-11 in the applicable forward-error metric, or when the compensated location/scale coordinate overflows. These are stated precision regions, not a claim that a wider arithmetic implementation is impossible. On the broad side, the opposite probability is evaluated as (t²+erf(|v|/sqrt(2)))/(1+t²), retaining the thin-side probability at the mode.

### Extreme d/p/q arithmetic

A finite centered residual can overflow when divided by the thin-side skew scale. The density then retains its logarithmic radius, and the probability uses the Student tail kernel in log-radius coordinates. This avoids squaring or materializing the unrepresentable standardized residual; unresolved extreme-skew centering errors remain separately recorded in the truth exclusions.

### Exact base-moment submodel

At nu=5 the standardized first absolute moment is 4*sqrt(3)/(3*pi). A two-word moment and compensated skew displacement retain the thin-side coordinate. The broad-side central probability uses the incomplete beta at v^2/(3+v^2); its linear branch has relative remainder bounded by v^2. The upper-tail hazard is bounded by 5/v for v>=1 and by 16 below one. The d/p bridge returns NaN if its practical coordinate margin fails or its raw displacement or standardized radius cannot be represented; these are named precision regions. Sampling and the inverse transformation retain their original arithmetic.

For other degrees of freedom, the first absolute moment uses a two-word half-shift gamma ratio. Its alternating Laplace expansion has remainder bounded by the first omitted term; recurrence reaches an argument of at least 32. Gamma log-convexity also bounds the difference from the normal moment by 2/nu, so the limiting constant is used only when that bound is below the two-word rounding margin. The symmetric member delegates directly to std.

### Relative conditional masses

A rare conditioning event can give a moderate conditional log density while both parent kernel terms are large. Positive Poisson ratios lambda/(k+1), anchored at the retained mode, remove that common kernel before normalizing; monotone ratios give a geometric bound on the omitted tails. Conditional evaluation returns NaN when its unit lattice cannot advance, its two-million-cell side guard cannot close the remainder, or a separated parent-log comparison exceeds its stated practical margin.
